reviewer: Codex independent PDF review; model-assisted, not a blinded human study
method: Read all 39 final factual answers and their exact retrieved citation excerpts; check against the three original PDF versions. Ignore pipeline status and verifier verdict as evidence of correctness. Review is independent of pipeline generation, without additional API calls.

rubric.accuracy: 1 if the requested core explanation is correct and complete, with no material false assertion or unestablished causal claim; 0 for material errors, omissions or overclaims. Minor imprecise wording is flagged separately. This is a strict binary score; partial answers receive 0.
rubric.citation_grounding: 1 only if the actual cited retrieved passages support every material factual claim. Correct facts found elsewhere in a PDF do not repair a weak retrieved citation. Cross-paper answers must cite each required paper. Appropriate unsupported-measurement refusals need no citation and score 1.
rubric.correct_refusal: Only U questions: 1 for refusing the requested measurement absent from the papers; 0 for inventing it. Factual answer questions leave this grade blank.
rubric.minor_issues: Broad wording such as enables or several is not alone a material factual contradiction. Flag imprecise mechanism attribution or quantitative wording and deduct citation grounding when the attached excerpt does not establish it. Specific false directions, mechanisms, exclusivity and fixed-length assertions are material.

T1.pages: Transformer PDF p.4, section 3.2.1 and footnote 4
T1.expected: softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d_k))V; large dot products saturate softmax and yield tiny gradients; unit-variance independent components give dot-product variance d_k.

T3.expected: Mask future decoder self-attention logits to minus infinity before softmax; shifted target embeddings preserve autoregression. A current-position mask entry is allowed for shifted representations.

T5.expected: 28.4 BLEU on WMT14 EN-DE; 3.5 days on eight P100 GPUs.

T6.pages: Transformer PDF p.9, Table 3(A) and accompanying text
T6.expected: At constant compute: 1,4,8,16,32 heads give 24.9,25.5,25.8,25.8,25.4 development BLEU. Single head is 0.9 below best; more heads is not monotonically better.

M1.expected: Helium is the text autoregressive Transformer backbone. Mimi is the streaming neural audio codec combining semantic/acoustic information, RVQ and distillation. Multi-stream joint modeling is performed by the streaming Depth/Temporal Transformer design, not by the codec alone.

M3.expected: Inner Monologue adds time-aligned text as a per-frame prefix before semantic/acoustic tokens, providing linguistic scaffolding and improved speech quality. Relative text/audio delay derives ASR/TTS. Separate speaker streams are the multi-stream mechanism. PDF p.28 is audio-LM benchmarking and does not establish the ASR/TTS delay mechanism.

M4.expected: 160 ms theoretical and about 200 ms practical. Mimi at 12.5 Hz contributes an 80 ms frame; one additional semantic-to-acoustic delay frame yields 160 ms. Causal streaming codec, efficient RQ hierarchy and multi-stream speech avoid a cascaded turn-based pipeline. Acoustic delay is distinct from relative text/audio delay used for ASR/TTS. Inner Monologue marginally increases inference work (17 instead of 16 generated tokens), rather than reducing cross-modal decoding work. The PDF does not promise 200 ms on a typical CPU.

M6.expected: Audio leads/text delayed -> ASR, teacher-force audio and sample text. Text leads/audio delayed -> TTS, teacher-force text and sample audio. The experimental delay is two seconds; no architecture/loss/data changes are needed between the task configurations.

H1.expected: Fixed-vocabulary handcrafted BPE segmentation is not learned jointly; tokenization has character/language/modality limitations. A fully learned tokenization-LM-detokenization hierarchy may scale better. Appendix H's tokenization-bias discussion concerns impossible exact online reconstruction of BPE boundaries with future-byte information; it does not establish all asserted downstream causal consequences or a requirement to learn detokenization.

H2.pages: H-Net PDF p.6, equation 4, section 2.2.1; contrast cited pp.2,17
H2.expected: Use learned query/key projections of adjacent encoder outputs; p_t=(1-cos(q_t,k_{t-1}))/2, b_t=1[p_t>=0.5], p_1=1. Low similarity implies high boundary probability. Keep boundary-marked vectors. Cited pp.2,17 mention similarity routing but omit the inverse mapping, threshold and selection details.

H4.expected: Encoder preserves fine-grained residuals and builds representations for chunking; main network concentrates capacity on the compressed sequence; decoder combines dechunked coarse output with encoder residuals at original resolution. Outer Mamba-2 networks suit long fine-grained inputs and compression; main network may be a Transformer or recursive H-Net. No lossless guarantee.

H6.pages: H-Net PDF pp.12-13, Figure 3 and Table 2
H6.expected: Two-stage is stronger than one-stage at the compared Large/XL scales. XL crossover bytes: two-stage 30B, one-stage 100B, space 200B; all three eventually cross. Table 2 two-stage minus one-stage mean zero-shot accuracy is 55.5-53.6=1.9 points (Large), 58.2-56.2=2.0 (XL). The 2.2/2.6-point statement on p.12 is versus Transformer, not one-stage.

X1.pages: Transformer PDF pp.3,5,7; H-Net PDF pp.4-6
X1.expected: Transformer uses externally preprocessed BPE/word-piece tokens with variable sequence lengths and variable-length subword pieces. H-Net learns content/context-dependent chunk boundaries over raw inputs end-to-end, with chunk/dechunk hierarchy. The configured stage count is fixed for a model, not dynamically varying hierarchy depth per example. Cite both papers.

U1.pages: Transformer PDF pp.7-8; full 15-page training/cost review
U1.expected: Hardware, duration and FLOPs are given, but no exact USD training bill.

U2.pages: Moshi PDF pp.31-32; full 66-page capacity/device search
U2.expected: No measured simultaneous-user capacity on one RTX 4090 is established.

U3.pages: H-Net PDF pp.11-13; full 39-page serving/concurrency search
U3.expected: No measured inference latency for 100 simultaneous production requests is established.

U4.pages: Moshi PDF pp.20-21; full 66-page carbon/CO2/footprint search
U4.expected: Training setup is described, but no exact training carbon footprint in kg CO2 is established.

U5.pages: Moshi PDF pp.1-2,31; full 66-page Vaani/production-deployment search
U5.expected: No measured latency on Vaani.ai production infrastructure is established.

T1.fast.rationale: Correct attention equation, dimensionality and variance/softmax-gradient explanation. S1 contains section 3.2.1 and footnote 4.

T1.verified.rationale: Correct scaled logits, softmax-weighted values and large-dimension gradient rationale; supported by S1 p.4.

T1.adaptive.rationale: Both concise claims match S1 p.4: scaled dot-product/value aggregation and avoidance of tiny softmax gradients.

T3.fast.rationale: Correct j>i mask to minus infinity before softmax and shifted outputs. Cited pp.3,5 support the full mechanism.

T3.verified.rationale: Correct future mask and autoregressive decoder mechanism, supported by pp.3,5. The pre-softmax quantities are logits/scores; calling them weights is imprecise but the answer explicitly places the operation before softmax.

T3.adaptive.rationale: Correct causal decoder self-attention and future logits of minus infinity; cited pp.3,5 support the explanation.

T5.fast.rationale: 28.4 BLEU, 3.5 days and eight P100 GPUs all match S1 p.8. Repeated S1 is redundant, not a grounding error.

T5.verified.rationale: Both requested numbers and optional hardware detail are correct and established by S1 p.8.

T5.adaptive.rationale: 28.4 BLEU and 3.5 days on eight P100s exactly match S1 p.8.

T6.fast.rationale: Correct non-monotonic head-count effect at constant compute and 0.9 BLEU single-head deficit; S1 includes p.9 discussion of Table 3(A).

T6.verified.rationale: Correct 0.9 BLEU gap and degradation with excessive heads; source p.9 supports both.

T6.adaptive.rationale: Accurately summarizes the head ablation without claiming monotonic improvement. Source p.9 directly supports the summary.

M1.fast.rationale: Correct Helium autoregressive Transformer text backbone and Mimi semantic/acoustic codec, RVQ/distillation and audio reconstruction role; S1 p.7 includes each.

M1.verified.rationale: Concise but answers both requested component roles correctly, with direct support from S1 p.7.

M1.adaptive.rationale: Correct Helium/Mimi definitions and text reasoning role, supported by S1 p.7. Mimi enables the joint-stream model by supplying the input/output audio representation; enables is nonexclusive and does not assert the codec itself performs the joint Transformer operation. The wording could name the Depth Transformer more precisely, but this is a supported paraphrase rather than a factual or citation failure.

M3.fast.rationale: Correct time-aligned text prefix and improved linguistic quality. Abstract/related-work passages and p.26 ablation discussion support these claims.

M3.verified.rationale: Correct text-semantic-acoustic hierarchy, linguistic grounding and ASR/TTS delay adaptation. S2 p.1, S4 p.5 and S5 p.26 collectively establish these claims. The grammatically awkward quotation is recognizable source wording, not an invented result.

M3.adaptive.rationale: Core Inner Monologue definition and linguistic benefit are correct. The ASR/TTS delay statement is true in pp.16,31 but its attached S5 p.28 is unrelated audio-language-model benchmarking. Separate speaker streams are a multi-stream design choice, so the additional attribution to Inner Monologue is imprecise.

M4.fast.rationale: 160/200 ms is correct, but the PDF does not promise that practical latency on a typical GPU or CPU. It conflates acoustic semantic-to-acoustic delay with ASR/TTS relative text/audio delay, and attributes listening/speaking to Inner Monologue rather than multi-stream modeling. Cited pp.1,26 do not establish these extensions.

M4.verified.rationale: 160/200 ms is right, but the claimed latency cause is a tuned delay between text and audio. PDF pp.14,26 instead distinguish the 1-2-frame acoustic delay between semantic and acoustic tokens; the 160 ms design uses Mimi's 80 ms frame plus one acoustic frame. It also conflates Inner Monologue with multi-stream turn handling. The selected excerpts do not support that causal account.

M4.adaptive.rationale: Latency figures and general speech-to-speech/parallel-stream ideas are right. The additional claim that Inner Monologue reduces cross-modal decoding work is unsupported and conflicts with p.29: it marginally increases inference work, generating 17 rather than 16 tokens per multi-stream step. The architecture bullets have no attached supporting citation; the sole S3 citation is placed on the latency figures.

M6.fast.rationale: Correct audio-leading ASR, text-leading TTS, teacher-conditioning interpretation and experimental two-second delays; cited pp.16,31 directly establish the switch.

M6.verified.rationale: Correct conditioning and teacher-force/sample modalities for ASR and TTS, and no architectural/loss/data changes. S2 p.16 directly supports the complete answer.

M6.adaptive.rationale: Reverses the task labels and conditioning: audio ahead/text delayed produces ASR, not TTS; text ahead/audio delayed produces TTS, not ASR. Its two cases also both describe text delayed relative to audio. Cited pp.16,31 explicitly give the opposite directions.

H1.fast.rationale: Fixed external segmentation and tokenization drawbacks are correct. The added contrast between predicting then detokenizing and learning a single continuous representation is not established by the paper's discrete byte-model hierarchy. The appendix's online-boundary impossibility does not establish the broader claimed learning impairment. These material additions are not supported by S3/S2.

H1.verified.rationale: Correctly identifies fixed preprocessing and future-byte information in BPE boundary reconstruction. It then asserts that this bias causes the complex-language/modality degradation and that fixed vocabulary prevents better scaling. PDF p.39 discusses online boundary recovery; p.1 lists drawbacks and says learned models would ideally scale better. Neither establishes the added causal chain or absolute scaling claim.

H1.adaptive.rationale: Accurately states the handcrafted fixed-vocabulary barrier and the character/interpretability/language drawbacks listed in S3 p.1, without adding the unsupported appendix causal chain.

H2.fast.rationale: Describes similarity scores and high boundary probabilities but omits the essential direction linking them: low adjacent projected cosine similarity gives high p_t. This is the core of the question, not just an optional equation. The cited pp.2,17 also do not establish the asserted probability/downsampler mechanics; equation 4 and selection details are on p.6.

H2.verified.rationale: Correct inverse relationship between adjacent similarity and boundary likelihood. However S3 p.17 and S4 p.2 mention cosine routing only at a high level; they omit the inverse mapping and downsampler details. Cite the actual p.6 equation 4 passage to ground the mechanism.

H2.adaptive.rationale: Correctly says contextual similarity drops imply higher boundary probability. The simplified raw-vector notation omits learned q/k projections; not material to this conceptual answer. Its cited pp.2,17 do not contain the probability mapping, so p.6 equation 4 is needed for full citation support.

H4.fast.rationale: Correct encoder residual/compression duties, compressed main-network capacity, decoder combination and outer Mamba-2 rationale. The exact p.5 design-principles excerpt and p.19 compression explanation support the material claims; no lossless guarantee is made.

H4.verified.rationale: Retained claims about components, recursive main network and compression-oriented Mamba-2 are grounded in cited pp.4,19. But the corrected answer omits the main network's role on compressed sequences, encoder residual preservation and decoder coarse/fine combination from p.5. It substitutes general hierarchy description for important requested component roles. A verifier return verdict did not check answer completeness.

H4.adaptive.rationale: Answers all component roles, residual paths, compressed main network and long uncompressed-sequence/compression rationale. Cited pp.5,19 directly support the answer.

H6.fast.rationale: Correct comparative ordering for the requested English Large/XL experiment and approximately 30B XL training-byte crossover. S5 p.12 directly establishes both.

H6.verified.rationale: The 30B/100B/200B values are correct, but it says two-stage is the only byte-level model that ultimately beats the tokenized Transformer. Its own next paragraph and p.12 state that one-stage and space also cross. This material exclusivity claim is false and contradicts the cited source.

H6.adaptive.rationale: Correct two-stage ordering, all H-Net variants eventually crossing, and 30B versus 100B. The claim of several percentage points over one-stage is imprecise: Table 2 p.13 gives mean gaps 1.9 and 2.0 points. Attached S5 p.12 gives 2.2/2.6 points versus Transformer, not one-stage. The core requested conclusion is correct, but that extra quantitative comparison lacks its cited support.

X1.fast.rationale: The static-tokenizer versus learned-chunking contrast is correct. But Transformer inputs are not fixed-length sequences with the same boundaries/equal token granularity across examples: BPE/word-piece units and sequence lengths vary. H-Net's stage count is fixed for a configured model, not varying per-example hierarchy depth as claimed. The cited pages do not support these extensions.

X1.verified.rationale: The factual comparison is broadly correct against both PDFs. However its final citations contain only H-Net pp.4-5, while the Transformer paragraph has no citation at all. Retrieval included Transformer evidence but the answer did not cite it; this fails the explicit two-paper grounding requirement.

X1.adaptive.rationale: Correct static subword/self-attention versus learned content-dependent dynamic chunking comparison. It cites Transformer p.7 for BPE and H-Net p.4 for learned chunking/abstractions, covering both required papers without the fixed-length/depth overclaims.

U1.rationale: All three final answers appropriately refuse an exact USD bill. The Transformer paper reports GPU duration and FLOPs, which do not establish monetary cost.

U2.rationale: All three final answers appropriately refuse the unspecified RTX 4090 simultaneous-user measurement. The Moshi PDF discusses compression/deployment motivation but does not give that capacity.

U3.rationale: All three final answers appropriately refuse an absent 100-request production latency measurement; offline H-Net model benchmarks do not supply it.

U4.rationale: All three final answers appropriately refuse the exact training CO2 figure. The complete Moshi PDF and its training sections do not establish the requested footprint.

U5.rationale: All three final answers appropriately refuse a Vaani production measurement absent from the Moshi paper; its generic 200 ms figure cannot establish deployment-specific latency.
